original.target_description: Original HILDA study of life satisfaction mean, variability, their interaction and mortality; row-specific predictor, adjustment model and contrast unresolved.

replication.target_description: Unassigned replication placeholder; outside completion scope.

notes:
Identity verified from supplied text: title matches Variability modifies life satisfaction's association with mortality risk in older adults; authors Julia K Boehm, Ashley Winning, Suzanne Segerstrom, Laura D Kubzansky; DOI 10.1177/0956797615581491; Psychological Science 26(7), 1063–1070 (2015). PMC author manuscript with Methods, Results, tables, Discussion and references, rather than abstract or secondary report. Supplemental PDF is referenced but not supplied. No PDF supplied; canonical web text lacks page breaks, so p. 4 cannot be independently mapped. Original locator is p. 4; study and outcome description are null. Multiple distinct predictors, adjustment models and simple main effects are reported. No evidence identifies this row with one test. Row order and numeric matching were not used. Common Table 2 model N candidate: 4,458 participants and 546 deaths in every model; retained only as a candidate because row correspondence is unresolved. Original cohort 19,914; excluded 14,789 younger than 50 and 667 adults aged 50+ with fewer than two life-satisfaction assessments. Final participants were aged 50+ at Wave 1 with complete satisfaction and death-date data. Missing covariates were multiply imputed in five datasets with estimates pooled; these are not independent participant samples. The 546 cases are deaths, not analytic N. No arithmetic-derived N assigned. Standardisation evidence: Both the mean and standard deviation of life satisfaction were standardized (

= 1) prior to inclusion in the statistical models. Table 2 models: 1 age; 2 demographic characteristics and health conditions; 3 adds smoking and physical activity; 4 adds depressive symptoms.
